title: Computer Environments Elicit General Agentic Intelligence in LLMs
data_curation: LLM-in-Sandbox-RL is trained exclusively on general, non-agentic context-based tasks: the seed data used to fine-tune the synthesizer in Instruction Pre-Training (Cheng et al., 2024), spanning encyclopedia, fiction, expert materials, academic tests, news, social media, and trivia. Each instance pairs background material (context) with related tasks of three types—free-form generation, multiple choice, and reasoning. Contexts are stored as files in the sandbox rather than the prompt; multi-document or long contexts are split into separate files (e.g., introduction.txt, methods.txt), and single-file contexts are augmented with distractor files sampled from the same dataset to force active navigation. No training data overlaps any evaluation benchmark. A data ablation contrasts this general data (placed in prompt vs. sandbox) against math data from DAPO and SWE data from R2E-Gym. Evaluation uses AIME25, UGPhysics, ChemBench, MedXpertQA, AA-LCR, IFBench, and SWE-bench Verified; test problems are reframed to prevent benchmark hacking via internet access.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. LLM-in-Sandbox-RL is a single-stage RL post-training applied on top of existing instruct models (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B); there is no multi-stage pretrain->SFT->preference pipeline. Within each training task, prior related tasks from the same instance serve as in-context examples while the model must explore the sandbox to complete a held-out testing task—a mild intra-episode ordering rather than a cross-stage curriculum. The authors advocate, as future work, folding computer-style reasoning into pretraining itself.
method: LLM-in-Sandbox virtualizes the computer as a lightweight Ubuntu Docker code sandbox with only basic functionalities (Python + NumPy/SciPy), exposing three tools—bash, file_editor, finish—in a ReAct-style multi-turn loop (Algorithm 1) until finish or a turn cap. Design is minimal (no domain-specific configs, one ~1.1 GB shared image) and exploratory (a prompt encouraging tool use and anti-hardcoding). LLM-in-Sandbox-RL is the core contribution: RL within this sandbox using only general context-based data, contrasting with LLM-RL (text-only, no environment) and SWE-RL (environment but domain-specific data). Training uses GRPO++ (the GRPO variant from DeepSWE/rLLM) with outcome-based, rule-based rewards—F1 for multi-choice, ROUGE-L for free-form, binary +1/0 for math—and zero reward for trajectories exceeding max turns/tokens. Trajectories are generated in LLM-in-Sandbox mode. The problem solved: whether computer environments elicit general intelligence and whether weaker models can be trained to harness them, with skills that transfer even to text-only LLM mode.
eval_metrics: Seven benchmarks across six non-code domains plus software engineering: AIME25 (30 problems x16, Math-Verify), UGPhysics (650, LLM judge), ChemBench (450, exact match), MedXpertQA (500, exact match), AA-LCR (100 x4, LLM equality checker), IFBench (300, rule-based loose), and SWE-bench Verified (500, rule-based). Headline metric is Delta = LLM-in-Sandbox - LLM. Training-free, strong models gain up to +15.5% (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, AIME25 math: 26.0->41.5) and +14.4% (MiniMax-M2, instruction following), while weak Qwen3-4B regresses. Long-context tokens drop up to 8x (Qwen 100K->13K); aggregate token ratio 0.5-0.8x; QPM ratio 0.6-2.2x (MiniMax 2.2x). After RL, weak Qwen3-4B flips to outperforming LLM mode (Biomed 14.4 vs 10.0; Instruction Following 37.7 vs 33.7) and even gains in pure LLM mode; capability-usage rates rise and average turns fall (23.7->7.0).
key_results: Training-free: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B on AIME25 math +15.5% (26.0->41.5); MiniMax-M2 instruction following +14.4%; long-context tokens cut up to 8x (Qwen 100K->13K). After LLM-in-Sandbox-RL, weak Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 outperforms LLM mode in sandbox (Biomed 14.4 vs 10.0; Instruction Following 37.7 vs 33.7) and also improves in pure LLM mode. Aggregate token ratio 0.5-0.8x and QPM up to 2.2x (MiniMax) at a ~1.1 GB shared image footprint.
evolution_note: Building on ReAct-style tool use, code-sandbox coding agents (SWE-agent, Claude Code), SWE-RL (DeepSWE, R2E-Gym), and Instruction Pre-Training data, this 2026 work isolates the computer environment itself as a source of general intelligence and shows general-data sandbox RL transfers to non-code domains and even text-only inference. It reacts to the surge of computer-equipped systems (Manus, Claude Code, OpenClaw) and motivates future 'computer-native' models where environment interaction becomes a first-class pretraining and RL objective for generalist agents.
